Not a flake in api/session.py — a latent bug in the test's tampering logic. It mutated the token's LAST character, which encodes the tail of the base64url'd HMAC: 20 signature bytes (160 bits) span 27 chars (162 bits), and the decoder ignores the 2 slack bits, so {Y,Z,a,b} all decode identically. The encoder only ever emits the canonical member (Y) of that class, so whenever the signature ended in Y, swapping in 'a' produced a different string with an identical decoded signature — verification succeeded and the assert failed. Rate = 1/16 reachable final chars; measured 1291/20000 (6.45%, 1-in-15.5) across varied timestamps, matching the reported ~1-in-15. No order dependence (hence the unreproducible --randomly-seed) and no timestamp boundary; the only per-run variable is the embedded timestamp changing the HMAC. Fix: mutate token[0], which always carries 6 significant bits. Verified 0/50000 accepted post-fix, plus 24/24 clean full-suite runs.

Fixed. The nightly built the site twice — build-output.data.test.ts builds it in a beforeAll, then the nightly built again — so it asserted against one tree and published another. Delivered; ADR 0018. Concurrent writers now share a build instead of each running one behind the flock. The soundness argument comes from 4oa: publish-notes.sh derives its keys from the committed store, so any build starting after my commit includes my note — which turns 'did my note publish?' into a question about ordering that a ticket counter answers. Builds are O(1) not O(N) (four concurrent writers cost two builds; forty also cost two) and the waiter's deadline is sized for two builds accordingly. The POST still blocks: coalescing removes the reason to revisit ADR 0007, since writers reach 'live' within a bounded wait instead of degrading into 'pending'. Two review passes hardened it — the running flag is lock-owned rather than inferred from Thread.is_alive(), every log goes through _safe_log (a raising logger would wedge the worker, or 500 a committed note from the request thread), and a failed Thread.start() degrades instead of raising. Concurrency is asserted with driven interleavings, not reasoned about. 148 API tests green; deployed and the service restarted.

Delivered; ADR 0019. Note the bead's stated AC was already met by beeatlas-4oa — build:content contains neither bundle step, and a src/ change makes the receipt stale so the fallback runs both. This delivered the unstated remainder: gating the bundle INSIDE a full build.

build:app is now a gate (scripts/build-app.mjs) that reuses the bundle when src/, both Vite configs, package.json, package-lock.json, .env* and the build id are unchanged and every manifest-named asset is present. Reuse is only checkable because beeatlas-96m removed the build clock; the proof is a byte-comparison of a skipped build against a vite-ran build (1668 files identical, same 15 filenames, 2 MB main chunk identical; only _scaffold-check's builtAt differs, as it does between any two builds).

The work was not the skip but the three side effects a skip must impersonate:
  1. emptyOutDir was the CLEANING BOUNDARY (ADR 0016) — the only thing that deletes from _site, which merge-swap then makes authoritative for the live site via --delete. A skip cleans everything except assets/.
  2. It made assets look FRESH. merge-swap age-prunes assets at -mtime +30 on the stated assumption of "new URLs each publish"; a reused bundle keeps old mtimes and rsync -a preserves them, so after 30 days of skips the prune would delete the LIVE bundle nightly, with a green build and a healthy ping. Fixed by touching what is reused; verified locally (aged 40d -> 0 over 30d) AND on maderas through a real publish (0 served assets over 30 days), with the rsync leg confirmed empirically (a mtime-only change transfers, >f..t...., and the destination ends up fresh).
  3. It emptied assets/ itself. A skip now deletes unnamed files AND emptied directories, comparing FULL relative paths — basename-vs-top-level-entry would delete a nested assets/species/ right after the presence check vouched for it, which is not hypothetical (validate-bundle-size.mjs has a branch for that shape), and an empty species/ sends that validator down a chunk-less branch and fails the build.

Two reviewers, and both earned their place: CodeRabbit caught a Windows execFileSync issue; Fable caught the merge-swap mtime bug (high, invisible to any content comparison), .env being an unfingerprinted bundle input (VITE_MAPBOX_TOKEN — rotate it and the gate would serve the revoked one indefinitely), and the git-HEAD input. The path-aware prune has behavioural tests in lib/bundle-assets.js + src/tests/bundle-assets.test.ts, replacing a grep-for-an-identifier test that could not distinguish a function existing from a function being called.

THREE DEVIATIONS FROM THIS ISSUE AS WRITTEN:
1. SIZE. '~20 MB measured' was a z0-10 figure. z0-11 raw is 200 MB. Two lossless transforms got it to 60.8 MB: round elevation to 1 m (200->92, worst case error 0.496 m, rounded not truncated) and lossless WebP instead of PNG (92->61, verified pixel-identical in MapLibre). z10 was built and compared side by side at 21.9 MB and rejected on looks -- ridges smear at z12. User chose z11 with the evidence.
2. LAYER POSITION. Not 'below the first symbol layer'. protomaps-themes-base interleaves fills and lines, so its first symbol layer is index 57; inserting there washes every road, trail and stream with shading in the one style that exists to make trails legible. Anchored under the 'water' fill instead: above earth/landcover/landuse_park, below water, streams, roads and all labels.
3. BUILD HOST. Not maderas. Unlike build-basemap.sh (a network extract), this is CPU-bound: ~11 tiles/min on maderas's 2 cores = ~3 h pinning the live web server, vs ~9 min on a laptop for a 61 MB upload. build-terrain-basemap.sh and the runbook now document build-locally-then-scp.

Verified in the real cascade rather than reasoned about: /species/Agapostemon/femoratus at a 390px viewport, strip grown to 9 thumbs, measured against the old rule as a counterfactual —
  flex-wrap: wrap   strip 134px tall (2 rows)   document.scrollWidth 390   no horizontal page scroll
  nowrap (old)      strip  64px tall (1 row)    document.scrollWidth 637   page scrolls sideways 247px
Renders 5 + 4 with no overflow.

Chose wrap over overflow-x: auto because this is a reference gallery — the reader compares body parts ACROSS the set, and a scrolling strip both hides that more photos exist and gives no affordance saying so. Cost is a taller card on narrow screens.
